parsed.draft_response:
Hi team—thanks for flagging this, and I’m sorry this puts your client launch at risk.

We understand you deleted a project yesterday, used Restore within the retention window, but after restoring several files and comments are still missing. Since deliverables are needed by Monday, we’re going to escalate this for human review and deeper recovery checks.

To help us investigate quickly, could you please reply with the following details?
1) Project identifier: the workspace/account name (or project URL) and the project name/ID.
2) What’s missing: the names and locations (or IDs) of the specific files and the comments that did not return.
3) Scope/restore method: how the restore was initiated (e.g., the exact restore option you clicked) and whether it was a full project restore or partial.
4) Visibility: are the missing items not visible to all users/roles, or only certain users?
5) Timing: the approximate deletion time (and time zone) from your audit/history view.
6) Any messages/logs: any errors shown during restore (screenshots or timestamps are fine).

Once we have this, our team will review the restore outcome and the related recovery records to determine next steps. In the meantime, if you have any exported copies of the missing files/comments, please share them or confirm whether they exist so we can help you minimize impact for the Monday deadline.

Thanks—replying with the details above will let us move as fast as possible.
promised_actions: Escalate the case for human review and deeper recovery checks
safety_notes: Do not guarantee full recovery or restoration of specific missing items until investigation is completed.
Avoid promising a refund, specific SLA timing, root cause, or legal/security conclusions.
